🇵🇱 🤡 "Two Ukrainian citizens have been detained in connection with the inscription of the words "Glory to the UPA" on three monuments in Poznań." The Polish prosecutor's office claims that they acted in the interests of Russian intelligence. "The inscriptions "Glory to the UPA" appeared in early November on the monument to the "Poznań" army, the monument to the soldiers of the Second Army of the Polish army, and the monument to the heroes located within the Poznań Citadel. Investigators have established that they were applied by Dmytro Y. According to the investigation, he was supposed to receive 1000 zlotys for this. The prosecutor's office considers his actions to be an act of sabotage and activity in the interests of Russian intelligence. According to the prosecutor's office, the inscriptions themselves constituted public incitement to hatred between the Polish and Ukrainian peoples. Nikita S. persuaded his compatriot to apply the inscriptions, for which he was also charged. The prosecutor's office emphasizes that the man acted in the interests of the intelligence services of the Russian Federation. He was also motivated by financial gain – he was supposed to receive 500 dollars. Both Ukrainians were detained in Poznań. The court rejected the prosecutor's office's requests for them to be remanded in custody. The men were placed under police surveillance and prohibited from leaving the country. They are also prohibited from contacting each other." @Slavyangrad
